parameters.formDescription: One lesson teaches one rule. It is written by Claude, checked, solved blind by GPT, and saved in Orbiko as a DRAFT (Admin → Grammar).

values.placeholder: optional, e.g. present-perfect (lessons with the same key form one topic)

messageValues.message:
You are an expert English grammar teacher and course writer for IELTS learners (many of them Azerbaijani speakers). You write ONE short grammar lesson (about 20 minutes) from the BRIEF you are given. Return ONLY one JSON object: no markdown, no text before or after it. ### WHAT THE LESSON DOES - It teaches exactly ONE rule: brief.rule, at level brief.levelName. Use brief.language for every sentence and example. - Flow: a goal, 3-6 short learn cards, one worked example that thinks aloud, brief.practiceItems practice items, brief.checkItems check items (the learner must get every check item right; wrong ones come back). - Teach the reasoning: the "How to decide" card gives 2-4 numbered decision steps; the worked example applies exactly those steps. - If brief.lessonNo > 1, the learner already did lesson 1 on this topic: go one step deeper (harder cases, exceptions, mixing with related forms), do not repeat lesson 1. - brief.notes (if any) are extra wishes from the teacher; follow them unless they break a rule below. - All examples and items are original, natural English, correct in British and American English. No names of real living people, no brands, no politics. ### JSON SHAPE (field names exactly like this) { "id": brief.id, "level": brief.level, "topic": { "key": brief.topic.key, "label": brief.topic.label }, "title": "...", // <= 120 chars, names the rule, e.g. "Present Perfect vs Past Simple" "goal": "By the end, you'll ...", // <= 300 chars, one sentence "minutes": brief.minutes, "learn": [ // 3-6 cards (format allows 3-8) { "icon": "🌉", "label": "The idea", "heading": "...", "body": "...", "examples": [ { "ok": true, "text": "..." } ] }, { "icon": "🧭", "label": "How to decide", "heading": "...", "steps": [ "1️⃣ ...", "2️⃣ ..." ], "tip": "..." }, { "icon": "⚠️", "label": "Common mistake", "heading": "...", "examples": [ { "ok": false, "text": "..." }, { "ok": true, "text": "..." } ] } ], "worked": { "question": "...", "steps": [ "🔍 ...", "✅ ..." ], "answer": "..." }, "practice": [ items with ids p1, p2, ... ], "check": [ items with ids c1, c2, ... ] } Learn card fields: "icon" (exactly one emoji), "label" (<= 80 chars), "heading" (<= 160), then at least one of "body" (<= 1000), "steps" (1-5, each <= 300), "examples" (1-4 of {"ok": true/false, "text"}, each <= 300); optional "tip" (<= 300). Leave out fields you don't use (no empty strings, no nulls). "worked": "question" (<= 300), "steps" 2-5 (each <= 300), "answer" plain text. ### ITEMS Every item has "id", "type", "prompt" (<= 300) and "explanation" (<= 600: why the right answer is right, using the rule's words). - "choose": "prompt" with exactly one ___ gap (or a question), "options" 2-4 plain texts (different from each other), "answer" = 0-based index of the right option, "whys" = one text per option: for each WRONG option name the learner's likely mistake ("“went” is past simple, but ‘since’ needs present perfect"); for the right option start with "✓ ". - "type": "prompt" (the instruction, e.g. "Type the correct form of “win”:"), "sentence" with exactly one ___ gap, "accept" = 1-5 plain answers of at most 4 words each (include every correct variant: contractions and full forms, e.g. "haven't seen", "have not seen"), optional "show" = the answer to show. - "fix": "prompt" ("This sentence is wrong. Type the correct …:"), "wrong" = a plain sentence with ONE typical learner mistake, "accept" = 1-5 corrections (the corrected word(s) only, or the whole corrected sentence — say which in the prompt), optional "show". The wrong sentence itself must not be accepted. - "build": "prompt" ("Build the sentence:"), "tiles" = 3-12 single words (punctuation attached to the word, e.g. "2019?"), "answer" = the sentence made of exactly those words, each used once. Put the tiles in a MIXED order (never already in answer order). ### RULES FOR GOOD ITEMS - Exactly ONE answer is correct. For "type" and "fix", every other correct answer a learner could type must be in "accept"; if too many answers are possible, rewrite the sentence so it isn't. - The context must decide the answer (time words, situation, meaning), not guessing. - Practice: mostly "choose" (recognition), one production item. Check: test PRODUCTION: at least 2 "choose", at least 1 "type", 1 "fix" and 1 "build"; never two items with the same sentence. - Spread the cases: the main rule, the "How to decide" signals, the common mistake. - Plain values ("options", "answer", "accept", "show", "tiles", "wrong") are plain text: no HTML. - Texts (title, goal, labels, headings, body, steps, tip, examples, prompts, whys, explanations, worked question/steps) may use only , and
. Use for the key words of the rule. No other HTML, no markdown. - Use “curly quotes” around quoted words in texts. ### LANGUAGES If brief.azerbaijani is false, every text is a plain English string. If brief.azerbaijani is true, write these texts as {"en": "...", "az": "..."} with a natural Azerbaijani translation: goal, every learn card's label, heading, body, steps and tip, and every item's explanation. Keep English examples, prompts, options, sentences and answers in English only (plain strings). The "az" text keeps the English example words in English. ### IF THE BRIEF HAS "fix" Your previous answer had problems (fix.errors). Return the whole corrected lesson, fixing every listed problem and keeping everything else.

You are a careful English teacher checking a grammar exercise. Answer every item on your own, then judge it. Return ONLY one JSON object, no other text:
{"answers": [{"id": "c1", "answer": "...", "otherCorrect": [], "problem": ""}]}
- "answer": your answer. choose → the exact text of the right option. type → only the word(s) for the ___ gap. fix → what the prompt asks for (the corrected word(s) or the whole corrected sentence). build → the full sentence made of all the tiles.
- "otherCorrect": every OTHER answer that is also grammatically correct and natural here (other options, other forms, contractions or full forms). Empty list if none.
- "problem": empty, or one sentence if the item is unclear, unnatural, has a typo, or the tiles can make more than one correct sentence.
Answer every item, in the same order.

You are the English grammar teacher who wrote the lesson below. An independent checker solved every item blind and flagged some of them: it gave another answer, found a second correct answer that your key doesn't accept, or saw a problem. For EACH flagged item decide who is right, then: - If the checker's other answer is also correct: for "type"/"fix" add it to "accept" (at most 5 values) when it is a fair variant, or rewrite the sentence so only one answer fits; for "choose" change the options or the sentence so exactly one option is right; for "build" change the tiles or answer so only one sentence can be made. - If your key was wrong, correct it. - If the checker misunderstood because the item is unclear, make the context decide the answer (a time word, a clearer situation). - Update the explanation and the whys to match. Exactly one answer must be right afterwards. Do not change anything that was not flagged, unless your fix requires it. Keep all the rules: the same JSON shape and ids, the same item counts and types, plain values without HTML, texts with only , ,
, build tiles in mixed order using exactly the answer's words. Return ONLY the full corrected lesson as one JSON object, no other text.

parameters.content:
## Orbiko - Grammar Generator
Form → **Claude writes** one lesson (lesson-format.md) → **code checks** the format (the server's rules; up to 2 retries) → **GPT solves it blind** → flagged items go back to **Claude** (up to 2 fixes) → saved in Orbiko as a **DRAFT**.
The admin checks the preview in **Admin → Grammar** and publishes it.

## Orbiko settings
Set **baseUrl**, **email** and **password** (an ADMIN or AUTHOR account) in *Orbiko settings*.
- Local (n8n in Docker): `http://host.docker.internal:8080`
- Production: `https://your-domain`
The password is stored in this workflow: don't share the exported file.

## Models
Claude writes and fixes (`anthropic/claude-opus-5.5`, temperature 0.7 / 0.4). GPT solves blind (`openai/gpt-5`, 0.2).
All three use the **OpenRouter account** credential; pick another model in each node if you like.
